claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified on the current record because aggregate readiness passes, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and public guidance permits certification if the limitation and monitoring posture are documented.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
Treat the weakness as material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Do not let product labels such as non-core or low-volume resolve materiality when named commitments or pending legal review exist.
Require evidence of resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before supporting certification.
evidence_requests: Approved risk-acceptance record explicitly covering the enterprise password recovery gap before launch.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
Release materials or model-card draft showing the required disclosure for the named launch use case.
Any policy-approved materiality assessment explaining why the named segment would not be treated as material despite the rollout commitments.
specific_concerns: The policy says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Admissible evidence says the enterprise password recovery segment misses target by 1.4 points and is named in two identity rollout commitments, which points toward materiality under the policy text.
The legal disclosure review is still open, so a required policy predicate appears unresolved.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance or of an actual completed disclosure decision before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support general readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure policy for a material named-use-case gap.
Public model-card and NIST-style guidance is generic and cannot override the specific internal release policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record without evidence of approved risk acceptance or completed disclosure for the named launch use case gap.
That documenting limitations and monitoring posture alone is sufficient under the stated release policy.
That the 5% projected traffic characterization meaningfully defeats materiality despite the policy text and named rollout commitments.
